parsed_output.subject: ted-eu:CPV-class:9261
parsed_output.target_actor_if_supported: Contracting authorities publishing CONTRACT_NOTICE and CONTRACT_AWARD_NOTICE notices under CPV class 9261 (division 92) in TED (EU public procurement)
parsed_output.observed_need: The packet establishes that contracting authorities published bounded sets of contract notices and contract award notices under CPV class 9261, with stated TOTAL_VALUE amounts (notice scope, EUR) that differ across notices within each set. Whether this reflects any underlying need, problem, or budget intent beyond the act of publishing is not established.
parsed_output.candidate_intervention_class: An information or analytics offering that aggregates and compares published CPV-9261 procurement notice values for contracting-authority or market-intelligence audiences
parsed_output.hypothesis_statement: It is worth testing whether contracting authorities that publish CONTRACT_NOTICE and CONTRACT_AWARD_NOTICE records under CPV class 9261 represent a class of actors with recurring procurement activity in this classification, such that an information/comparison service built around published notice values could be relevant to them or to parties monitoring this activity. This is not established by the packet and requires further observation of buyer identities, recurrence across time, and any stated need.
parsed_output.independence_status: Independence is UNKNOWN for 6 of 6 rows in this packet. This does not establish that the evidence rows are independent findings; the row count is a count of published notices, not of independent observations.
parsed_output.reliability_status: All 6 rows are SCORABLE, meaning a reviewed reliability applies to every measurement. Scoring-ready is not the same as scored, and no score exists for any row in this packet.
parsed_output.evidence_bound_reasoning_summary: The packet establishes only that TED published bounded sets of CONTRACT_NOTICE and CONTRACT_AWARD_NOTICE records classified under CPV class 9261 (division 92), with stated TOTAL_VALUE amounts at notice scope in EUR that differ from one another within each set (spans of 15,658,679.12 across 3 notices, 235,017 across 2 notices, and 86,827,200 across 6 notices). Per BT-161, TOTAL_VALUE includes options and renewals and is not realised spend, a price, or willingness to pay. Publication of a notice establishes that a contracting authority exists and acted, supporting BUYER_OR_BUDGET_EXISTENCE, and the presence of stated monetary values supports ECONOMIC_VALUE and MARKET_ACTIVITY in the narrow sense of published notice activity. Nothing here establishes recurrence by the same authority, any need or dissatisfaction, existing or absent solutions, distribution channels, regulatory drivers, feasibility, or willingness to pay for any product. The narrowest defensible hypothesis concerns whether the actors publishing these notices constitute a class worth further observation, not that any need, market, or demand for an intervention exists.
critical_uncertainties: Whether the same contracting authority appears more than once across these notices, which would be needed to establish recurrence rather than a one-off count.
Whether any contracting authority has expressed a problem, need, or dissatisfaction with any current approach in this CPV class.
Whether any existing solution serves this need, and if so, how adequately.
Whether the published TOTAL_VALUE figures correspond to any actual expenditure, since BT-161 includes options and renewals and may be lawfully withheld.
Whether any actor would pay for an information or analytics product built on this data.
Whether a reachable channel exists to reach these contracting authorities or any other audience interested in this data.
Whether this activity is trending up, down, or stable, since no time-series comparison is supplied.
